title: package.json scripts for a dependency free project
when: A Node project needs a package.json, consistent commands to start, develop and test, or the user asks how to run the project.
prompt:
Goal: A minimal valid package.json whose scripts call only Node, so the project runs right after cloning with no installs.
Steps:
1. Fields: name (lowercase, hyphens), version "0.1.0", description, "type": "module", "private": true unless publishing, license, "engines": { "node": ">=20" }.
2. Scripts: "start": "node server.mjs", "dev": "node --watch server.mjs", "test": "node --test", plus tasks like "build": "node scripts/build.mjs".
3. Move anything longer than one command into scripts/*.mjs instead of shell syntax that differs between systems (&&, rm, cp, export).
4. For a CLI add "bin": { "toolname": "bin/toolname.mjs" } and a "files" list.
5. Omit dependencies; if one seems required, say so in README instead of adding it. Document each script there in one line.
Quality bar:
- Valid JSON: no comments, no trailing commas.
- Every script runs in any shell.
- Script names use the usual verbs: start, dev, test, build.
Pitfalls:
- rm -rf or cp in scripts; use fs.rm and fs.cp in a Node script.
- Inline variables (PORT=4000 node ...), which some shells reject.
- A placeholder test script that always fails.
Verify:
- [ ] The JSON parses.
- [ ] name, version, type and test exist.
- [ ] Each referenced file exists.
- [ ] No dependencies block.
Output: package.json at the project root and a Scripts section in README.md.

examples.input: como eu rodo esse projeto? cria o package.json
examples.output: package.json with type module, engines node >=20, start, dev with --watch, test with node --test
